gap: No result ChatGPT got states how far each camera can sit from the gate it releases or what that link needs: JAGER PRO's built-in transmitter reaches a M.I.N.E. control-box receiver at most 50 yards away, and new receivers must be on channel 5. The $599 camera-only listing cannot drop a gate unless that receiver is there, and on a non-JAGER trap the receiver only comes in the $1,800 conversion kit. AnywhereCam's Wireless Trapper uses its own transmitter and receiver with a 9 V relay, and the 9 V battery is not included.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited pages: jagerpro.com M.I.N.E. Live Stream, hogtraptrigger.com and hogeyecameras.com. I also checked the uncited JAGER pairing and conversion-kit pages from ChatGPT's own results. None of the cited pages gives a camera-to-gate distance, a pairing requirement or a list of what is excluded. The JAGER Live Stream page names only the M.I.N.E. Gate and never mentions the control box. HogEye's page says only 'Works on Any Trap'. Hog Trap Trigger says it 'works with any camera' but names no carrier. The 50-yard limit and channel-5 rule appear only on JAGER's pairing help page, which ChatGPT got but did not cite. ChatGPT's own line 'Requires a compatible gate controller' is not on the page it cited, and it gave no price for that controller.
decides: For a shopper who already owns a trap that is not a JAGER trap, the $599 JAGER camera alone will not work. The JAGER path really costs $1,800, as the conversion kit with control box, latch and live-stream camera, and the gate must be within 50 yards of the camera. AnywhereCam's Eagle 4G Wireless Trapper Edition costs $557 and includes the camera, transmitter, receiver and relay. It is the cheapest complete retrofit we could source, but its radio range is unpublished and it takes about 2 weeks to build. HogEye's kit uses a 30-ft wired gate cable, so the camera has to sit close to the gate.
